tasks.gr8-development-of-the-self-in-society-t: Topic: Development of the self in society. Cover self-image, self-concept, self-motivation, strengths, support systems, and personal goal setting. Ask Grade 8 learners to reflect on identity, recognise influences on self-esteem, and choose practical actions that build confidence and responsibility.
tasks.gr8-relationships-and-emotional-wellbein: Topic: Relationships and emotional wellbeing. Cover peer pressure, bullying, abuse, communication, assertiveness, warning signs, and help-seeking. Ask Grade 8 learners to choose safe responses in scenarios, identify trusted support channels, and apply respectful communication in friendships.
tasks.gr8-study-skills-and-personal-organisati: Topic: Study skills and personal organisation. Cover time management, homework routines, concentration, planning, and independent learning habits. Ask Grade 8 learners to build simple study timetables, select strategies for common learning problems, and reflect on improving consistency.
tasks.gr8-physical-education-task-t1: Topic: Physical Education Task. Cover warm-ups, basic fitness, invasion-game skills, safety, fair play, and teamwork. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify safe movement routines, choose cooperative game decisions, and recognise behaviours that support participation and skill development.
tasks.gr8-sexuality-feelings-values-t1: Topic: Sexuality: feelings, values, pressure and respect (Grade 8 Life Orientation, Term 1). Values-based and age-appropriate only: normal feelings in the teenage years, feelings against actions, influences (friends, family and community norms, culture, media), respect, consent as respect, saying no, and where to get reliable information and help (trusted adult, teacher, clinic nurse, Childline 116). Do not describe anatomy or sexual activity. Ask the learner directly (you), never about learners or CAPS.
tasks.gr8-relationships-friendships-t1: Topic: Relationships and friendships: starting, keeping and ending (Grade 8 Life Orientation, Term 1). Cover starting a friendship, signs of healthy friendships (trust, respect, honesty), constructive disagreement with I-messages and compromise, ending an unhealthy friendship safely, and who to tell (trusted adult, Childline 116). Ask the learner directly (you).
